title: Personality Was Robust to the Transition to Remote Work Under the COVID-19 Pandemic.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The current study examines whether the transition between work contexts (in-person work to remote work) during the COVID-19 pandemic influenced an individual's personality in a sample of 1475 working adults. Previous work on personality change during the COVID-19 pandemic suggests that people experienced a significant change in personality.
METHOD: Drawing from the personality dynamics literature and frame-of-reference effects, we extend this work by conducting IRT-based invariance analyses and by fitting linear mixed-effects models on longitudinal, archival data.
RESULTS: Results indicate that transitioning to remote work did not affect either interpretations of personality items nor mean-level personality trait scores during the COVID-19 pandemic.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings from the current study suggest that while many aspects of work and non-work life changed in 2020 and 2021, we did not find evidence that the pandemic and the sudden shift to remote work influenced personality assessment. Findings also provide support for the established theory that personality is robust to situational changes, highlighting the robustness of personality to predict future behaviors and attitudes regardless of changing work contexts.
